/usr/bin/unix_chkpwd.purpose: PAM shadow/account verification in the native authselect stack; retain for authentication and owner-recovery validation.

/usr/lib/polkit-1/polkit-agent-helper-1.purpose: Privileged PAM authentication for native polkit/run0 elevation.

/usr/bin/arping.purpose: Network diagnostics are owner/root operations; networkd uses its own authorized sockets.

/usr/bin/clockdiff.purpose: Raw-socket clock diagnostics are owner/root operations; authenticated time has a separate daemon.

/usr/bin/chage.purpose: Local account expiry is owner/root policy; human accounts use homed.

/usr/bin/chfn.purpose: Human account metadata is managed through homed; local account maintenance is owner/root only.

/usr/bin/chsh.purpose: Human login-shell policy is managed through homed; local account maintenance is owner/root only.

/usr/bin/gpasswd.purpose: System group administration is owner/root only; human membership is managed through homed.

/usr/bin/mount.purpose: Host mounts are owned by PID1 or explicit elevated owner maintenance; no unprivileged fstab user mounts.

/usr/bin/newgidmap.purpose: Native trusted namespace brokering performs mappings; unprivileged external subordinate-ID helpers are outside this host contract.

/usr/bin/newgrp.purpose: Human group policy is managed through homed; privileged group-changing shells are unnecessary.

/usr/bin/newuidmap.purpose: Native trusted namespace brokering performs mappings; unprivileged external subordinate-ID helpers are outside this host contract.

/usr/bin/pam_timestamp_check.purpose: The selected native PAM stack does not use pam_timestamp authentication caching.

/usr/bin/passwd.purpose: Human password changes use homectl; local recovery-account changes require explicit owner elevation.

/usr/bin/pkexec.purpose: Native run0/polkit is the host elevation path; this alternative executable gains no implicit privilege.

/usr/bin/su.purpose: Native run0/polkit is the host elevation path; root may still change identity deliberately.

/usr/bin/umount.purpose: Host mounts are owned by PID1 or explicit elevated owner maintenance; no unprivileged fstab user mounts.

/usr/libexec/qemu-bridge-helper.purpose: Native nsresourced supplies an authorized TAP descriptor; QEMU has no host network-administration capability.
